In honor of Jarrod Bunk’s belief that the bike community can help to build a community in need, we bring back Higher Ground with the locals of Johnstown, the Pennsylvania Environmental Council, and the Community Foundation for the Alleghenies.

This will be a scenic tour with opportunities to connect with the natural beauty of the Laurel Highlands and bond with like-minded souls before and after in downtown Johnstown.

The goal is to keep the grassroots spirit of the original iterations of Higher Ground which showcased rugged routes throughout the surrounding Johnstown area. Expect to be greeted with punchy climbs, path-less-travelled trails, and a tour of the environmental wonders that are the Laurel Highlands and the Allegheny Mountains. 

Here are the routes that will be available:

  • Thirty: An out-and-back on the Path of the Flood and Staple Bend Tunnel trails to go to the Johnstown Flood Memorial Park (you'll ride through the dam that broke).
  • Forty: Heads north towards Hinkston Run Reservoir, then east on quiet paved roads before bombing down into Summerhill and into the Johnstown Flood Memorial Park (you'll ride through the dam that broke), and returning to Johnstown on the Path of the Flood and Staple Bend Tunnel trails.
  • Sixty: Does the Forty route back into Johnstown, then up into the Rager District climb & descent, and back into Johnstown.
  • Eighty: Does the Forty route back into Johnstown, and then UP into the forested Gamelands west of town and then back down to the rolling roads in the south before riding back to on the Jim Mayer Riverswalk and into Johnstown.
  • Hundo: Does the Forty route back into Johnstown and then UP into the forested Gamelands west of town and then back down to the rolling roads in the south before riding back to on the Jim Mayer Riverswalk to the Start/Finish and the last 20 miles go up into the Rager District climb & descent and back into Johnstown.

There will be aid station support and the start/finish venue will have food & drink available. All riders must check in & out so we know who's taking on which sections of the course.

To learn more about the history and purpose of Higher Ground, read this story on The Radavist from 2022.

Partners that are making Higher Ground happen include:

  • Pennsylvania Environmental Council
  • Community Foundation for the Alleghenies
  • Fat Jimmy's Outfiters
  • Thomas Automotive
  • New Trail Brewing
  • Endo TuneUp
  • Stan's
  • Nittany Mountain Works
  • Footdown.cc
  • Freeze Thaw Cycles
  • Hushmoney Bikes

Proceeds from Higher Ground will support The Women's Help Center and the Pennsylvania Interscholastic Cycling League.

PLEASE NOTE:

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  all registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Additional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $30 for Juniors for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table.

This page will re-open for late/day-of registration by Saturday 10/24 at 8:30 AM.  Check-in at the venue will open around 7:30 AM on event day.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race. There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

 Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license (or a printed Authorization to Ride) showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Code of conduct: Racers and spectators are expected to abide by USA Cycling's code of conduct. Any behavior, sign, kit, etc., that discriminates on the basis of race, color, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation, gender identification, or national origin, or that interferes physically with any race, will be met with ejection from the venue and disqualification from all races.

Gender Equality & Transgender Policy: Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. The minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; please see the current USAC Rulebook for minimum Racing Age and categories for Women.  The Super Series  welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy

The collective teams comprising the MABRA Super Series are committed to providing inclusive and equitable racing events.  The Super Series is proudly adding non-binary categories (1/2/3 and 4/5) to race during the women's races.  This addition is to honor all of our cyclists and provide a category that allows everyone to race with how they identify.  In the event that USAC chooses to amend current policy to align with UCI changes for our transgender racers, then WTF (women-trans-femme) will be added to our non-binary categories as WTFNB.

Start Staging: Cat 5 Men & Cat 4/5 races = Registration order (HURRY…the first race is on BikeReg!). All other fields: Super Series standings for first row (8 racers), Crossresults.com for the rest of the field. Be at start staging 15 minutes before your race start or risk losing your spot.

Series Points:  Weekly Super Series points are awarded for ranking to the following fields – Men Cat. 1/2/3; Women Cat. 1/2/3; Masters 40+ Cat 1/2/3; Masters 50+ Cat. 1/2/3/4; Masters 60+ Open; Master Women 45+/50+/60+, Cat. 1/2/3/4; Men Single speed Open; Women Single speed Open; U19 Junior Women and U19 Junior Men. Youth Categories will receive overall series point leader jerseys following the last race @ Cap Cross Classic.

See the BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series website for complete rules and regulations for series points.  Points calculated at Crossresults.com.

Directions: Once arriving at the fairgrounds entrance, follow the parking volunteers to the designated parking area. Parking of vehicles or trailers will not be permitted in the team pits. Traffic is one-way only! You will enter and go right down the road to the parking area. Once leaving the parking area you will exit on opposite side you entered and leave going left up the hill. Please follow the signs.

On-Course Warmup: Riders shall only enter the course for warmup laps between races in the designated area near the starting grid.  Race officials will designate time and length of pre-rides.

Pit: There will be one double-sided pit on course. Please remove your equipment immediately following each race to make room for others. UPDATE - ONLY valid USAC license holders may enter the pit and provide support for racers. No spectators or non-licensed persons will be allowed in the pits. Please see a USAC Official if you have questions.

Course Description: The course will utilize multiple areas of the fairgrounds, including grass, pavement, dirt, gravel, barns, the ever so fun happy humps and barriers. There may even be a surprise or two!

Welcome to the Second Annual Endgrain Coffee Roasters Cyclocross race held in historic Alcyon Park!

 

Multi-Race discount now in place! Add a second race for just $20

 

Due to a century old town by-law, all events must take place after 12:00pm on Sundays, hence the late start times. 

The course will consist of a mix of grass, a small section of paved walking path, and a good chunk of the wooded disc golf course. Feedback from 2025 was taken into account some small changes will be made including but not limited to: No turns on the disc golf tee boxes, additional tape in the woods, possible relocation of the finish if we can find a good spot.

 

Helmets must be worn at all times and absolutely zero alcohol consumption on borough property. 

Registration will open an hour before the first race, day of registration is available, cash only. Promotor has the right to combine categories based on registration numbers, etc.

Licensing Requirements:   This is a USA Cycling sanctioned event. All riders must present a valid license at registration and sign an event release form (minors must have a parent/guardian sign).  One-day and annual licenses will be available for purchase at registration. Junior discounts only applicable to junior race fields. Current USAC Fee Schedule here. https://usacycling.org/memberships-old/one-day-licenses

Call-up Protocol:  Call ups will be given based on NJBA Standings and rules. Above all we will use promoters discretion. If you yell at the promoter you will go to the back. 

Lapped Riders:  Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders.  Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and are not to interfere with their progress or trail behind them. Laps are pretty fast on this course, and come in around 7-8 minutes. 

Results:  Results will be posted at the registration area.  Results will be made final 15 minutes after being posted.  The top 3 finishers in every event must report immediately to the start/finish line for awards and photos.

A quick and dirty rendering of what the course is going to look like: Some off-camber stuff, INTO THE WOODS WE GO, back out to a 180 degree log over situation, then into the sand, loop out around the playground, then a smooth ride around the warning track of a ballfield, rinse repeat as many times as the officials see fit.

NOTE: E-BIKE MEN AND WOMEN CATEGORIES – THIS IS WILL BE A SPORT CLASS CATEGORY AND WILL FOLLOW SPORT CLASS COURSES/DISTANCES

E-BIKE REGULATIONS (THIS IS A WORK IN PROGRESS....LEARNING AS WE GO....)
As we continue to provide e-bike racing in the Month of Mud series we want it to be a safe but welcoming racing environment for all mountain bike enthusiasts and racers. In order to do so we believe the following standards are fair for our local grassroots series.
 
• E- Bikes that are USAC UCI or GNCC certified are legal.
• E-Bikes must pedal assist with a max speed of 20mph.
• Programmable E-Bikes must be set and locked to 750 watts and 20 MPH. • Throttle mechanisms are prohibited. • Boost buttons must be removed or disabled. • No aftermarket modifications will be allowed.
• E-Bikes must be inspected 30 minutes before the race start. • E-Bikes MUST be in the off position at the starting line and powered up at the official's instructions. • Settings must be verified immediately after finishing. • Any E-Bike that is found to be illegal, rider will forfeit all prizes and points and will be suspended for remaining races. All categories. • Officials carry the right to test any E-Bike in question. Month of mud is not liable for any damage that may occur during testing. If you withhold your E-Bike to this test, you will be disqualified from the race.
• Passing etiquette must be followed. Unsportsmanlike behavior, foul riding, use of profanity, or flagrant discourtesy directed at participants, spectators, or officials will result in disqualification.
• Analog bikes have the right of way, you must yield to a racer in a different class to pass you when appropriate and safe to do so.
• No battery swapping during the race

PLEASE CHECK INDIVIDUAL RACE EVENTS ON BIKE REG, WEBSITE AND FACEBOOK GROUP FOR RACE TIMES & MORE DETAILS AS EACH RACE APPROACHES.
www.monthofmud.com

Lastly, this is the MoM, let's have some fun!

Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 8:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 6:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: JUMP BASICS & JUMP PROGRESSION SUN OCT 25th
EventNotes:
The Ride Series is different. Your expectations should be high as you enter the hospitality of our classroom setting. A comfortable Kijaro chair awaits your presence and the cover our 10x20 tents provides reprieve from the elements. Prepare yourself to be immersed in an environment that provides the perfect opportunity for you to be open to embracing and practicing the proper technique. Instant feedback from our coaching staff will have you progressing like never before! Are YOU ready??

 

 

 

JUMP BASICS: 

We get it, everyone wants to jump! However, most people don't embrace the technique AND psychology behind doing it well. You have to understand the what and why before you can start to build confidence with the how, that's what this session is for. Not only will you build a solid understanding of what NEEDS to happen, you'll also get plenty of reps working through the steps of how it needs to happen, all in a safe and controlled environment. 

Topics Covered: 

Riders will get plenty of reps on multiple takeoffs/landings and Rich will work through multiple rounds of video so you can see exactly what's working and what isn't. 

JUMP PROGRESSION Session: Ground School and Skills Park Jumpline

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Our Pro level coaches break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 70 years experience, they guide you through their real world experience and give you key insight and cues on what to do and also what not to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get tons reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

REGISTRATION NOTES: 

  • Online registration closes at 11:59PM on Friday prior to race day.

  • No refunds due to buyer's remorse/if you are unable to attend.

  • In the unfortunate event that we are forced to cancel the event due to COVID, inclement weather, or other circumstances beyond our control, the race director will seek to refund entry fees, but cannot refund BikeReg fees.

  • 2nd Race Only $10 if you register in the same transaction. You pay full price for the more expensive race.

  • No outside alcohol will be permitted! Alcohol and food will be available for purchase at Sycamore Speedway. 

LICENSES: All races will be held under USA Cycling (USAC) permit. Riders without an annual USAC license will be required to purchase a 1-day license for $15. Renew your annual license online at http://www.usacycling.org/.

All USAC rules apply. Helmets must be worn at all times.

EventNotes:
Adventure Cycling Association is celebrating 50 years of bicycle travel in 2026. To mark this milestone, we invite you to join the 50TH ANNIVERSARY DROP-IN RIDES, a celebration across three legendary routes.

WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF THE DROP-IN RIDES?
Drop-In Rides are part of Adventure Cycling’s 50th Anniversary. Just as Bikecentennial ’76 sparked a movement 50 years ago, these rides celebrate where we started, what we’ve accomplished, and where we’re going—inviting riders everywhere to share in the adventure.

THE ROUTES
TRANSAMERICA TRAIL – The original Bikecentennial ’76 route that launched Adventure Cycling. Nearly 4,200 miles from Oregon to Virginia, it passes through small towns, farmland, the Rockies, and Appalachians. Dropping in here connects you with the history of cross-country cycling.

GREAT DIVIDE MOUNTAIN BIKE ROUTE – Since 1998, the world’s premier off-pavement route. Over 2,700 miles of gravel, dirt, and rugged mountain passes from Montana to New Mexico. A true test of endurance and adventure, inspiring riders worldwide.

GOLDEN GRAVEL TRAIL – Created for our 50th Anniversary, debuting in 2026. A mixed-surface journey across plains, canyons, and mountains, designed to showcase America’s growing gravel culture and the future of bicycle travel.

WHERE CAN I LEARN MORE ABOUT THE ROUTES?
Visit our route overview pages to see descriptions, maps, and details to help you choose the ride that fits your goals:

  • Great Divide Mountain Bike Route overview
  • TransAmerica Trail overview
  • Golden Gravel Trail overview (launching early 2026)

HOW DO I GET MY ROUTE AND NAVIGATE IT?
Adventure Cycling offers both paper maps and digital maps for purchase:

  • TransAmerica Trail Maps
  • Great Divide Maps

These maps include turn-by-turn directions, service listings, and detailed navigation notes. Once downloaded, digital maps can be used offline on your GPS device or phone.

Golden Gravel Trail Maps – This brand-new 50th Anniversary route will be free to download starting early 2026.

For more information about digital maps, visit our Digital Routes FAQ.

HOW CAN I FIND A GROUP TO RIDE WITH?
Check out our Companions Wanted listings to connect with others planning to ride.

Adventure Cycling members can post on Companions Wanted (become a member, just $2.50/month), while anyone can respond to a post. Drop-In Rides have a dedicated section in Companions Wanted in celebration of our 50th Anniversary.

EventName: 2026 I Love Gravel Racing Points Series
EventNotes:
2026 I Love Gravel Racing Points Series

Everyone, Everywhere, Every distance

3 distance categories

Short = 24 miles or less, Mid = 25-49 miles, Long = 50+ miles

 

A different approach to a Points Series. There will be 2 categories, Male and Female, no age group, NO E-BIKES. Must be a GRAVEL RACE. No minimum or maximum number of races. No specific races, but Premier Races benefit the participant with double points.

For 2026 we have added Clydesdale and Athena categories. In addition, we will have the Fat Tire and Junior categories that were added in 2025. These categories will have a registration fee of $20 and do not include the opportunity to win FREE, or discounted, race entries. It does include your opportunity to win trophies, swag bags and your private invitation to the Champions Celebration. All details for these new categories are listed below.

Our goal is to increase participation in gravel racing. We are not looking for the fastest Champion. We would like our Champions to be passionate, and engaged, in the gravel racing community. With that thought in mind, the person who participates at more races stands a greater chance of being Champion.

Series will run from March 1, 2026 and end on November 1, 2026. You may sign up for the Series at any point throughout the year, but your points will not count until AFTER you have signed up. No retro results.

**Race results reporting are the responsibility of the participant. Participant must report their results to ILGR through an email (ILoveGravelRacing@aol.com) with a verifiable source, such as timing service or results documentation. Results must be reported within 2 weeks of race completion AND by November 1, 2026.**

$25 fee for registration will include your chance at the Championship. You are not locked into one distance. Your registration will allow you to compete in EVERY distance. 

Points will be awarded for your Overall Male or Female finish at ANY GRAVEL RACE, ANYWHERE. However, we have a group of Premier Gravel Races where double points may be earned. Since we have membership internationally, you may race anywhere, at any distance and participate in this Series.

2026 Premier Races are:

3/28/26 Melting Mann in Jones, Michigan

 4/25/26 Waterloo G & G in Grass Lake, Michigan

5/2/26 Black Fork Gravel Grinder in Glenmont, Ohio

5/23/26 Roughneck Gravel Roubaix in Titusville, Pennsylvania

 8/8/26 Frankenmuth Fondo in Frankenmuth, Michigan

 8/15/26 Fast Fitty in Charlotte, Michigan

8/29/26 Thunder Bay Thriller in Alpena, Michigan

9/13/26 Uncle John's Dirty Ride in St. Johns, Michigan

9/19/26 The Dirty Mitten Gravel Race in Middleville, Michigan

10/4/26 Rode to Hell in Chelsea, Michigan

10/24/26 Lowell Classic Fall Gravel in Lowell, Michigan

Points rundown: 1st Overall = 500 points, 2nd = 495, and so on. 101 place Overall through infinity will receive 5 points for completing ANY gravel race. 50 points are earned if someone signs up for the Points Series and you are listed as their referral. 10 points are earned for every race that you start and list ILGR as your team. More referrals, more points. More listings of ILGR as your team, more points.

Awards:  1st Male and Female in each distance will receive a custom Champion jersey, awesome trophy and 11 FREE entries to Premier Races in 2027.

2nd Male and Female in each distance will receive an award and 50% off entry to 11 Premier Races in 2027.

3rd Male and Female in each distance will receive an award and 25% off entry to 11 Premier Races in 2027.

All winners will receive incredible swag bags.

EVERYONE who registers for the Points Series is entered in drawings with more prizes throughout the 2026 race season!!

Junior Category will be a Trophy category. The Top 3 places will receive awards, swag and an invite to the Champions Celebration. This will be a Coed division covering 12 years old and under. One distance category of 24 miles or less. The same point standard will apply. Premier races will be worth double points. Your points will be determined by Overall Junior placement. In the event of a tie, your Premier Race points will be the determination. This category is a separate registration fee from the standard Points Series.  You may enter both. 
 
Fat Tire Category will be a Trophy category, like the Junior Category. It will be a Coed division that will encompass ANY age. Any distance between 1-49 miles will be the category. Top 3 will receive awards, swag and an invitation to the Champions Celebration. The same point standard will apply.  Premier races will be worth double points. There must be a Fat Tire Category for your points to be awarded in this category. Your points will be determined by Overall Fat Tire placement. In the event of a tie, your Premier Race points will be the determination. This category is a separate registration fee from the standard Points Series. You may enter both.
 
Clydesdale and Athena Categories will be a Trophy category. Clydesdale definition for ILGR Points Series is Male weighing 220 lbs. or more. Athena definition for ILGR Points Series is Female weighing 165 lbs. or more.  It will encompass ANY age. Any distance between 1-49 miles will be the category. Top 3 will receive awards, swag and an invitation to the Champions Celebration. The same point standard will apply.  Premier races will be worth double points. There must be a Clydesdale/Athena Category for your points to be awarded in this category. Your points will be determined by Overall Clydesdale/Athena placement. In the event of a tie, your Premier Race points will be the determination. This category is a separate registration fee from the standard Points Series. You may enter both.
 
To allow more people to enjoy our Champions Celebration, we will offer the opportunity for you to purchase tickets to attend. This process allows EVERYONE who wants to share in these special moments to be included.

The Big Bear Lake Trail Center is quickly becoming known as the hot spot for classic east coast single track. Years of trail development, by experienced mountain bikers have created a trail system that will have you grinning ear to ear. The terrain has everything to offer; gradual climbs, large embedded rocks, tight slaloms, challenging rock gardens, and off the saddle downhills. Almost 50 miles of trail wind through knee deep ferns, soft needle pine plantations, and groves of mountain laurel. Riders of all ages and abilities will find trails to fit their individual riding skills and need for adrenaline. The Big Bear Lake Trail Center is the place to bring the entire family to experience mountain biking at its best.

We make it easy to find your way around. Trail maps will be mailed to online season pass purchasers or you can ask for one at the main entrance.  We also suggest checking out the TrailForks app or the MTB Project app on your mobile device. All trails may be used for hiking, trail running, and x-c skiing. Trails are closed from November 1 thtough December 31. Trails are open from January 1 to October 31 each year.

NOTE:  The team t-shirt order is placed early in the year, typically the cut off is the middle of March.  If you do you register and order your shirt by the cut off date, you will not be guaranteed a t-shirt.  The registration fee does not change after cut off.  So please register early.

The Turkey Burner will be the final stop of the Big River Gravel Series! The event will take place from Camp Liberty which sits on 245 wooded acres positioned in some of the best gravel riding Iowa has to offer. There are enough cabins on site to sleep 275 riders! We have a rustic heated shelter in case the weather is less than ideal. Last year, riders could not get enough of this venue. After finishing, there will be a post race party to celebrate another successful year of gravel riding and our new running series. 

Cycling Routes- 

The routes will not be marked so please make sure to download the route to your cycling computer or print off the cues. Looking for more information, check out our website bigrivergravel.com for further details. The event will be held rain or shine. There are no refunds or deferrals. BikeReg does offer registration insurance at checkout. Every cycling participant will get a slice of Casey's pizza, some pumpkin pie, and a beverage of their choice.

Looking for lodging?

The Turkey Burner takes place from Camp Liberty, a 245 acre Girl Scout Camp which has several accommodations ranging from primitive tent camping to a lodge that sleeps 14!

The series takes place in the Quad Cities which is located on the Iowa Illinois border, nestled between the Mississippi River and Rock River. 

The series consists of four events

Hell of the Wind- March 28th, New Liberty, IA

1904- April 25th, Morrison, IL

Burning Quad- July 11th, Erie, IL

Turkey Burner- October 31st, New Liberty, IA

For detailed information on each event, check out their respective Bike Reg page or our website bigrivergravel.com for further details. 

Gravel Riding Series Competition-

For the first time ever, the Big River Gravel Series will have an overall series payout for the top 3 men and women in the Mississippi distance. In order to be eligible for the payout a rider must sign up for the entire series using the Big River Gravel Series registration page. It is a dynamic payout. If 50 or less riders register for the Mississippi distance series the payout will be $500. For every rider who registers for the Mississippi distance once over 50 riders, the payout increases by $50 per rider registered. Example- 100 total riders register for the Mississippi distance series, the payout would be $3,000. 

Riders must decide if they want to compete in the Mississippi River (long distance) or the Rock River (short distance) for the series and stick with that distance for the entire series. If a rider switches distances, their points will start not carry over to the new distance series competition. 

The Big River Gravel Series will have an overall series payout for the top 3 men and women in the Mississippi distance. In order to be eligible for the payout a rider must sign up for the entire series using the Big River Gravel Series registration page on BikeReg. The rider must also finish all 4 events.

There will be a series competition for overall (women/men) in each distance, age group (women/men), and a single speed open. Riders are eligible for both point series competitions. 
 
There will be a podium for top three overall (women/men) in each distance and top three in each age group (women/men). Riders are eligible for both the overall and age group podium.

Age group categories are divided as follows. There will be an age group category for women and men. 19 and under juniors, 20-44, and 45+. 
 
Scoring for the overall and age group categories will work as follows. 1st= 10 points, 2nd= 9 points, 3rd= 8 points, 4th= 7 points, 5th= 6 points, 6th= 5 points, 7th= 4 points, 8th= 3 points, 9th= 2 points, 10th= 1 point

Scoring for the series will be based on a riders accumulative points from all 4 events. 

A rider must complete at least 3 of the 4 events to be eligible for the series. 
 
In the event of a tie at the end of the series, the tiebreaker will be determined by the rider who had the best result at the Turkey Burner.

Let’s run it back. If we aren’t racing for pies, are we really even racing? Lucky for us, we won’t have to wonder any longer as Bishops Orchards, True Cyclery, and the NHBC are thrilled to present the Orchard Scorcher Sunday, November 30. For the second year running, this course will twist and turn around the blueberry orchard, the apple trees, and maybe even the corn maze at 480 New England Rd., Guilford, CT 06437. Looking forward to seeing you there.

Important Event Details

  • Please take note of the venue address! This race will not take place at the main Bishops Orchard Farm Market, for those of you that have raced this event in the past. The race will take place at their Blueberry Picking location (don't worry, it's still an apple orchard too!) located at 480 New England Road.
  • Pre-ride available on Saturday November 29th. Please sign up if you are interested in pre-riding the course on Saturday 11/29.  The course will be open between 12 pm - 3 pm. The property is gated, so you will not be able to access the course before 12 pm and you must be done with your pre-ride by 3 pm.  See the course map below!
  • Sadly, no dogs this year. As bummed as we are to leave our fur-babies at home, Bishops Orchard does not allow dogs due to their status and regulations they are under as a working food producer.
  • Parking is on site. There should be plenty of available parking when you pull into the venue. If not, there will be an overflow lot provided.
  • Food and Drink! We will keep you satiated with food and drink throughout the day. Minnow Coffee & Matcha will be there in the morning selling espresso-based drinks! The Caseus Crispy Melty Food Truck  will be on site early as well to offer up breakfast, grilled cheese sandwiches, and soups to keep you toasty warm! Additionally Bishop's Orchard will have cider (hard and not-hard) for sale on site.  So come hungry and show our food partners some love on the day of the event!  
  • Bring your friends and families! We are planning to have a jungle jim made of tires to climb on, a separate kids track, music, and food for the day, so invite your friends and family along to come cheer the racers on.
  • Staging for all fields is determined first by Project Mayhem CX series point (available here) for the front row and then by crossresults points for all pre-registered participants. Day-of registrants (effective after we assign bibs on Saturday, Nov 29th at 12 pm) will be staged at the back. Staging will start 15 minutes prior to each race, please be on time. If you miss your call up, you will be staged at the discretion of USAC Officials! 

Discounts, Refunds and Fee Schedule

  • PLEASE REGISTER EARLY! It's the single biggest thing you can do to help us make sure the race is ready for everyone that ends up coming!
  • Price goes up to $50 for senior fields and $30 for junior fields and beginner series on Sunday November 23rd and $10 more on Saturday, November 29th at 12 pm. So again…sign up early!
  • First 20 riders to sign up for the Women 5 (Novice) and 4/5, and Nonbinary 5 (Novice, race in Men/Open 5), and NB 4/5categories get FREE REGISTRATION with code GNARFreeEntry! Courtesy of Richard Sachs (thank you thank you thank you!)
  • Wanna race multiple fields at the Scorcher? Please sign up for both at the same time and pay only $20 for each additional race!
    • Already signed up for one race but want to hit a second? Or third? OR FOURTH?? Use coupon code: TwoRaceHero
      • Please note that if you use this option and are racing on a One-Day USAC license, bikereg will charge you for another one-day and (as far as we know) there is nothing we can do to prevent that from happening, so please sign up for both at the same time if you can!
  • Full refunds (minus bikereg fees and one-day license cost) granted through Friday, November 28th
  • Bibs and call-ups will be assigned at 12:00 pm on Saturday November 29!! So if you want to make sure you get a good call up (let's say it all together this time!) make sure you SIGN UP EARLY!

EventNotes:
Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 8:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 6:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

EventName: Tacchino Ciclocross -- Event #7 of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series
EventNotes:
The Venue:  we have an exciting venue -- the Montgomery County Agricultural History Farm Park, which provides us with lots of terrain and options for fun and challenging cyclocross features.

Parking:  parking will be adjacent to the course. Look for signs at the entrance.

Alcohol Prohibited!  The venue is a Montgomery County park.  Park regulations prohibit alcohol. Please do not jeopardize our use of the park.

Food Trucks:   There will be at least one food truck and we are working on more. 

Medical/First Aid:  There will be EMT support on-site.  First aid will be available at the registration shelter. 

The Event:  Tacchino Ciclocross is a BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series event.  The event is held under USA Cycling permit #16399.  All USAC Cyclocross rules apply. Event will be held rain or shine.  Prizes will be awarded as soon as possible after each event.  Please remain near the podiums following your race if you place.  The start of the protest period will be announced. 

Course Description:  The course will be classic Mid-Atlantic.  There are rolling hills, a challenging section through the woods, numerous off-cambers, gravel paths, and at least one set of obstacles.  There will be one double-sided pit on the course.

****PROFESSIONAL CHIP TIMING by Insight Timing Services****

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  all registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Addtional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $25 for Juniors for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table. 

This page will re-open for late/day-of registration in the afternoon of the Friday prior to the event.  Race day registration and check-in will open by 7:30 AM.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 20 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

Series Points:  SuperSeries points are awarded for all races EXCEPT the Novice Men and Cat. 4/Novice Women races.

On-Course Warmup:  riders shall only enter the course for warmup laps between races in the designated area near the starting grid.  The gate will be the only entry point to the course and entry time will be designated by the race officials.

Staging:  riders shall be staged in order of their assigned bib number.  Tacchino CX is the 7th event of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross SuperSeries.  In fields eligible for SuperSeries points, bibs will be assigned to the first 8 riders (i.e., the front row) in order of their position in the Super Series standings on CrossResults.com ( https://www.crossresults.com/superseries ); remaining riders will be assigned bibs in order of the riders’ CrossResults.com ranking points; any remaining unranked riders will be assigned bibs by registration date & time.  For the Novice Men & Cat. 4/Novice Women, riders will be assigned bibs by registration date & time.  For all race categories, the first 4 positions in the third row are optionally available to the Race Director for discretionary call-ups.  Race day entries will be assigned remaining bib numbers on a first come, first served basis; riders registering on race day are not entitled to special treatment based on their position in the SuperSeries points standings or their CrossResults.com ranking.

Staging Procedure:  riders will fill the starting grid by bib number, 8 riders at a time, as specified in the USA Cycling Cyclocross rulebook when so directed by the officials; the officials will fill any gaps left by DNS or late-arriving riders as appropriate.  ALL RIDERS MUST ASSEMBLE IN THE PRE-STAGING CHUTE NO LATER THAN 10 MINUTES BEFORE THEIR START!   Riders arriving late to staging may be staged at the back of the starting grid at discretion of the Chief Referee.

MABRA Mission Statement:

“To promote the sport of bicycle racing in the Mid-Atlantic region, principally within the states of Delaware and Maryland, the northern portion of the state of Virginia, the eastern panhandle of West Virginia, and the District of Columbia;

To foster camaraderie and fellowship among culturally, racially and gender diverse bicycle racers and enthusiasts within the Mid-Atlantic;

To help ensure bicycle racers and enthusiasts in the Mid-Atlantic have an equal opportunity to participate in bicycle racing and activity without discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation, or national origin;

To support and facilitate the efforts of its members, clubs, and other organizations that promote diverse, inclusive and equitable bicycle racing/activity/engagement in the Mid-Atlantic;

To support the efforts of its members in promoting bicycle racing and events for local, regional, national and international competition; and

To undertake such actions as are necessary, proper, desirable, advisable, or convenient for the furtherance and accomplishment of the foregoing purposes, provided that such actions do not exceed the bounds accepted for a District of Columbia nonprofit corporation.” 

* The 150 rider limit is for the combined field in a race.  Registration will close once the limit has been reached by any combination of classes within the field. 

* Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. Minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; minimum Racing Age and categories for Women per USAC rules.

** Promoter reserves the right to increase total prize purse as race day gets closer.

Gender Equality & Transgender Policy: 

Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. The minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; please see the current USAC Rulebook for minimum Racing Age and categories for Women.  The Super Series  welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy

The collective teams comprising the MABRA Super Series are committed to providing inclusive and equitable racing events.  The Super Series is proudly adding non-binary categories (1/2/3 and 4/5) to race during the women's races.  This addition is to honor all of our cyclists and provide a category that allows everyone to race with how they identify.  

In the event that USAC chooses to amend current policy to align with UCI changes for our transgender racers, then WTF (women-trans-femme) will be added to our non-binary categories as WTFNB.

Event contact information: 

www.squadracoppi.org 

https://www.facebook.com/squadracoppi  

Race Director:  Tom Faucette 202-360-6886

Thanks for reading, and see you on race day!

Calling all mountain bikers! It’s time to cap off your season with some adrenaline-pumping, late-season racing.

Why ride?
Shake off those post-Thanksgiving calories with a thrilling ride through the crisp, frosty woods of Ringwood State Park. The course is designed to challenge your skills while giving you the perfect mix of fun and competition.

Prime conditions, unbeatable vibes!
Late November riding in New Jersey? Absolutely! With the shifting weather patterns, early December now offers fantastic, fast conditions for mountain biking—cold enough to keep you cool, but not too icy to stop you from tearing up the trails.

Whether you're looking to set a personal record or simply enjoy one last race before the year ends, Frosty Woods MTB is where you want to be. Don’t miss your chance to ride, race, and celebrate the season in style!

Double Shot Race

Single Shot Race

By popular demand we've added this special one lap race. Perfect for fitting in your training plan or making it your 1st MTB Race!

No USA Cycling License Needed

Podiums & Post Race Party

We'll have podiums with medals, raffle prizes plus Dave's famous Turkey Chilli and Danette's Vegetarian Lentil Bean Soup plus Athletic Brewing NA Beer and more.

Want to get an idea of what you're going to need to podium?

Here's the 2024 Frosty Woods MTB Results

The Course

We've created a fast and flowy course that's different from the one held in the Spring. 90% Singletrack & Good Fun!

All families joining a CCAP Program are required to adhere to CCAP Protocols.  These are found in the waivers section of the online registration form on BikeReg.  Please review and confirm with your signature.

WCC Membership 2026 

WestCoast Cycling Society (WCC) has been primarily a mountain bike club for many years, but with the reduction in XC racing and activity, we have transitioned into a road, gravel and Cyclocross focused group.  We still do mountain biking, but opportunities for racing are somewhat limited.
A previous requirement for membership with WCC was a Competition License or General Membership with Cycling BC (CBC).  Since 2025, this requirement has been dropped.  We no longer require a CBC membership or license to join WCC. There is no distinction between licensed and non-licensed members.
WCC is officially affiliated with CBC, the benefit of this is that we can put on races under the stewardship of CBC.  This requires that at least one member of WCC must hold a Competition and Technical License with CBC, a condition that we do indeed meet.

There is always support for anyone that wants to organize an event, a ride or an adventure that club members can participate in.  Some that come to mind …. weeknight Mt.  Seymour Road climbs, a mid summer Mt. Baker climb (followed by burgers or ice-cream), North Shore Mountain bike epics and local gravel escapades.

More General benefits for WCC membership. 
-  Opportunity to join and connect with members for recreational and racing opportunities
-  No charge (as in free) entry into any racing events organized and run by WCC.  Club members all chip in to help organize and run events as well as race (the primary objective).  Vanier Park CX is our primary event focus.
-  We have a great relationship with Schwalbe Tyres which results in us being able to order great tires to keep us all running rubber side down, all with a decent discount.   https://www.schwalbetires.com/
-  Blonyx Canada has been good enough to support our members with a 25% Discount on their nutrition and supplement products.  The discount code is sent out monthly and can be paired with they existing 15% subscription discount.  I can vouch for the electrolyte and the protein powder (NO Stevia …. yipee).    https://blonyx.ca/
-  While limited in scope, we also have a sponsorship arrangement with RaceFace Easton for discounts on parts and accessories.  Again, it helps with keeping our bikes running and up to date.      https://www.raceface.ca/

EventNotes:
Please visit the West Texas Showdown website for more information about this event and routes.  

West Texas Showdown

Terlingua, TX | Dec. 4th - 6th, 2026

The West Texas Showdown isn’t just a race — it’s a battle against the desert itself. Big Bend delivers jagged singletrack, endless horizons, and conditions as raw as they come. Wild, unpredictable, and unforgiving — this is where legends are made.

The third stage of the Texas Showdown Series and the crown jewel of the Texas Showdown Triple Crown.  Set in the Big Bend region of Texas, this event promises to test every ounce of grit, skill, and determination.

This is mountain desert country — wild, remote, and raw. The terrain is rugged, the weather unpredictable, and resources are scarce. Nearly everything in the desert either bites, pinches, stings, or grabs. Don’t be scared — but don’t come unprepared.

Big Bend – Home of the Showdown

Big Bend Ranch State Park and the surrounding desert country embody the spirit of West Texas: wide-open basins framed by volcanic cliffs, deep canyons carved by the Rio Grande, and horizons that shift with every mile.

It’s one of the most remote places in the lower 48, where solitude comes naturally and silence is as striking as the scenery. Out here, self-reliance isn’t optional — it’s survival. By day, the desert unfolds in stark beauty: ocotillo stretching skyward, hidden springs tucked into arroyos, and dirt roads that climb to vistas you’ll never forget. By night, you’ll ride under one of the darkest skies in North America, the Milky Way blazing overhead in a show few places on Earth can match.

Event Options

Showdown – 390 miles of Glory & Pain
This is the flagship route: long, raw, and unrelenting. It starts with a paved rollout from Terlingua before plunging straight into the wilds of Big Bend Ranch State Park. Riders will grind up gravel park roads, hike through rugged arroyos, and battle through stretches of singletrack where “rideable” depends on your skill, stamina, and stubbornness.

Highlights:

  • Marfa (Mile ~200): A quirky West Texas art town, home of the mysterious “Marfa Lights” and the famous Prada “storefront.” Will quite literally be a desert oasis for riders.
  • Pinto Canyon: One of the most dramatic landscapes in Texas. A twisting, jaw-dropping descent through volcanic cliffs. Sunrise or sunset here is unforgettable.
  • Rio Grande Stretch: Long paved miles along the border, with Mexico just across the river. Stunning views and a glimpse of life in the small border towns.
  • The Death Loop: A 50-mile finale north of Terlingua that will test what’s left of your legs and your willpower.

Stats: ~390 miles | 60% unpaved / 40% paved

Slowdown – 290 miles of Dust & Determination
A shorter, but still fierce route through Big Bend. The Slowdown trims the distance but keeps the character: gravel park roads, rough country tracks, stretches of arroyo riding, and just enough singletrack to keep you honest. This is a full-on bike expedition into one of the harshest and most beautiful places in the country.

Highlights:

  • Remote gravel stretches deep inside Big Bend Ranch SP
  • Rough, sandy arroyos that force you to wrestle with your bike as much as ride it
  • Expansive desert views that make every climb worth it
  • Just enough pavement to catch your breath before the dirt pulls you back in

Stats: ~290 miles | 48% unpaved / 52% paved

Lowdown – The Gateway to Big Bend
 The Lowdown is our non-competitive, guided bikepacking group ride. Designed to introduce riders to the magic of Big Bend in a slightly more approachable way. This route is not to be taken lightly, the distance is shorter, but the miles are hard. A good option for those with experience bikepacking, but want to try something more extreme.

Ride leaders and sweepers will help guide the way, but this is still a self-supported trip. You’ll need to carry your own food, water, and camping gear. Along the way you’ll experience the vastness, solitude, and starlit skies that make Big Bend unforgettable.

Highlights:

  • Long stretches of gravel roads and dry arroyos inside Big Bend Ranch SP
  • Nights spent under some of the darkest skies in North America
  • Bring your big tires and probably suspension

Stats: ~85 miles over 3 days | 80% unpaved / 20% paved

Schedule

Thursday, Dec. 3rd

  • 12–8pm: Rider check-in & tracker pickup
     
  • 8–9pm: Pre-race meeting at TBD

Friday, Dec. 4th

  • 7am: Showdown & Slowdown & Lowdown - Grand Departs

Saturday, Dec. 5th

  • All day: Ride Your Damn Bike

Sunday, Dec. 6th

  • All day: Celebrate finishers at Temple of the Bird
     
  • 5pm: Hoedown starts w/ live local music
     
  • 7–8pm: Awards + raffle
     
  • 10pm: Party winds down
     

Host City & HQ

Our host town is Terlingua, TX — a once-thriving mercury mining hub turned ghost town, now home to a small but eclectic community of artists, adventurers, and desert dreamers. Nestled between Big Bend Ranch State Park and Big Bend National Park, Terlingua’s ruins, shacks, and quirky dwellings create a setting unlike anywhere else.

Race HQ will be at the Temple of the Bird and it'll be our home for the weekend.

Getting Here

Terlingua is off the beaten path — there are no direct planes, trains, or buses. The nearest airports are in Midland or El Paso; from there, it’s a long desert drive. If you’re arriving via Alpine or Marfa, you’ll also pass through a Border Patrol checkpoint before reaching town.

Rider Notes

  • Bike Choice: This is MTB country — rocky climbs, rugged singletrack, arroyo crossings, and rough gravel. Leave your gravel bike at home.
  • Self-Supported: Riders must carry food, water, navigation, and repair gear. Resources are extremely limited.
  • Leave No Trace: The desert is fragile. Pack it in, pack it out. No catholing. Carry a waste bag.
  • Risks: Remote terrain, wildlife, weather extremes, and isolation. This is not an event for the faint of heart or the unprepared.
     

FAQ

Why don’t the routes go into Big Bend National Park?
Bikes are not allowed on singletrack trails inside the National Park. All riding is on roads only. Big Bend Ranch State Park offers far better opportunities for rugged, off-road adventure.  The National Park is also not open to these types of events…yet!

Will I pass through a Border Patrol checkpoint?
Yes. If you’re driving in from Alpine or Marfa, you will pass through a permanent Border Patrol checkpoint north of Terlingua. Have your ID handy.  You will also have a Border checkpoint if you are doing the Showdown or Slowdown heading into Marfa.  

What’s the weather like in December?
Riders should be prepared for temperatures ranging from below freezing overnight to warm, sun-filled afternoons. Weather in Big Bend Ranch State Park can change rapidly, and strong winds, cold rain, and freezing temperatures are all possible. Conditions may vary dramatically across the route due to changes in elevation, terrain, and exposure.

? What bike should I bring?
This is MTB terrain. Wide tires, suspension, and durable gear are highly recommended. Gravel bikes will not cut it here.

? How self-supported is this event?
Completely. Riders are expected to carry their own food, water, tools, and navigation. Resupply points are limited, so plan carefully. Rescue vehicles will be available to extract riders off course if needed, but when you're riding, you're on your own!

? How do I handle waste?
Big Bend’s desert ecosystem is delicate. Riders must follow Leave No Trace principles. That means packing out all trash and carrying a waste bag — no catholing allowed.

The legendary New England Cyclocross Finale Returns for its 19th year!
 

 

49% of extremely biased twitteratti agree:  this race is basically the World Championships


Hey, you probably noticed from the category names that this isn't a USAC sanctioned event.   If you can't figure out what field to register for, the answer is either "Beginner" or "Singlespeed."  Or you can always email us any questions using the "contact event" link above.  

 

What's with the name?:

It's a combination of this and that.


Who races when??  How do I win money? 

  • Jedi Men and Jedi 40+ Men will race together (1 start) with 40+ denoted in results.  Shared prize list of $500 with $100 bonus cash for 40+.

  • Jedi Women and Jedi 40+ Women will race together (1 start) with 40+ denoted in results.  Shared prize list of $500 with $100 bonus cash for 40+

  • Singlespeed men, fat bikes and women will race together (2 starts) with separate results and prizes.

  • Riders can race in additional races for $20.

  • Start positions determined by rider rankings at crossresults.com

  • Mountain Bikes allowed in any category.  Even if they have bar ends.  Unless the bar ends have pointy knives on them.

What's new this year?

We have a food truck (Thai Chili)!  

There's a bunch of new weird motocross lines and piles of dirt to play with!  We don't know exactly how we're going to use it all yet, but we do know it's gonna be good.

What's your inclusivity policy?

Ice Weasels is a celebration of cyclocross that everyone should feel welcome to be a part of.  Athletes are encouraged to show up and and race as their authentic selves in whatever category makes the most sense to them.

We have a zero tolerance policy for harassment so if anyone is being a jerk about anyone's identity (or anything else for that matter) let us know and we'll take care of it.
 


What's your refund policy?

We grant all refunds, all the time, for any reason.  Missing the race is punishment enough, we don't need to rub it in by keeping your money.  If you're on the fence, just register now (before your field is full!) and ask for a refund if you change your mind.

 

Remember how awesome last year was?

Welcome to the Pie Ride!

Keo, Arkansas • Saturday, December 5, 2026

Nestled in Southern Lonoke County (SoLoCo), Keo is a bike-friendly town of just 207 residents that knows how to roll out the welcome mat. We’re glad you’re here to ride, celebrate, and of course—eat pie!

Routes

  • SoLoCo 25

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/52192236

  • SoLoCo 35

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/52192137

Start Line

The ride begins at 10:00 AM sharp from the Keo Airstrip on Pecan Road. The airstrip is located just half a mile east of town at the intersection of Pecan Road and Cemetery Road.

Pre-Ride Happy Hour

  • When: Wednesday, December 2
  • Where: Moody Brews 414 E. 21st Street, Pettaway Square, Little Rock, AR.
  • Time: 4:00 PM – 7:00 PM

We are celebrating Happy Hour at Moody Brews and want to introduce you to a really cool partnership between the brewery, South Lonoke County (SoLoCo) and the Pie Ride! Moody Brews gets their rice for their New Ground Pils from Isbell Farms, located in SoLoCo. Brewer Josiah Moody then transforms that rice into New Ground Pils, a light lager, which will be served at the Pecan Festival. We are going green this year and only providing a bib number, safety pins and a drop bag to be used on ride day. Drop your street clothes at the start line and they will be at the Finish Line to change into for the Festival. 

Did You Come to Get Your Nuts Cracked?

Grab the official 2026 Arkansas Pecan Festival tee! Printed on soft, 100% cotton, lived-in Comfort Colors shirt in green. This year's festival tee is one you'll actually want to wear long after festival day.  

$30 each - Sizes S-XL

Pre-order yours and pick it up at the Pre-Ride Happy Hour at Moody Brews, Wednesday, December 2nd or on festival day, December 5th, in Keo. Last day to order a shirt is November 30th.

Ride Morning

  • Check-In: Look for the Keo Collective at the Airstrip. They’ll get you to the start line on the runway. *Note, there will be a single toilet available at the Airstrip, please plan accordingly, extra facilities available a half mile west at the Festival.
  • Drop Bags: Write your name clearly on your bag and place any post-ride clothes or gear inside. Volunteers will transport it to the official Finish Line in downtown Keo at the Arkansas Pecan Festival. 

Finish Line Celebration

The ride officially ends in Keo, right in the heart of the Arkansas Pecan Festival. Secure your bike in the secure bike area, grab a Moody Brews pour, and savor your well-earned slice of pecan pie. Stick around to enjoy the festival’s car show, vendors, entertainment, and holiday cheer.

Important Note: You must register before November 23 to guarantee your slice of pie is reserved for you at the Finish Line.

After the Festival

When you’ve had your fill of pie and fun, noodle back at your own pace to the Keo Airstrip to retrieve your vehicle. Don’t forget to collect your drop bag with your kit, helmet, and shoes before heading out.

This is the first time the Arkansas Downhill Series will be hosted at the OZ Trails Bike Park and there couldn’t be a better finale to the Arkansas Downhill Series! This DH will be an intense, solitary race against the clock that gives riders a legendary experience. Racers descend the park’s beautifully crafted trails at the absolute edge of control, balancing raw speed with the mental challenge of line choice.

Registration opens Friday, June 12th at 8am with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding enduro race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation. 

Each participant’s entry includes:

  • Registration includes lift access during Practice, Seeding, and Finals
  • Sufficiently marked courses with map emailed to participants the week of the event.
  • Aid stations with access to professional neutral mechanics and medical support.
  • Professional event timing with accuracy to the 1,000th of a second and instant results.
  • Complimentary post-race meal and cold beverages (21+ for adult beverages, ID required) in a family-friendly festival setting.
  • Awards ceremony by category with prizes awarded 3 deep.

RACE VENUE

OZ Trails Bike Park

Race Venue Address - 2852 Bella Vista Way, Bella Vista, AR 72714

EVENT SCHEDULE

Final event schedule with packet pickup, official pre-ride, and start times will be released the week of the event. ARDH events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances.

  • 1pm-2pm | Timing Chip Pick Up for All Categories

  • 12pm-12:30pm | Wave 1 Chip Pick Up

SAFETY - This is not the time to skimp on protective equipment. Helmets are required to be worn on course during official event times and we highly suggest a full-face helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads.

TEMPERATURE - In Bella Vista, Arkansas, December is relatively mild but chilly, with average daily highs in the upper 40s to low 50s (9°C to 10°C) and average overnight lows dropping into the 30s (0°C to 1°C)

WATER & SNACKS - While hydration will be available at select locations on course, riders are encouraged to plan to carry at least 50-60 ounces of water and enough snacks to sustain themselves under strenuous exercise.

NICE TO HAVES - Bug spray, sunscreen, spare tubes, pump or CO2, plugs, patches and other parts.

DOGS - Dogs are allowed but are required to be on a leash at all times. No exceptions.

TRASH - If you pack it in, pack it out. We are guests. Please follow all event sustainability and recycling requests.
